review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ σκανδαλισθῆτε.
16:1.targetText: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.

16:2.sourceText: ἀποσυναγώγους ποιήσουσιν ὑμᾶς· ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα ἵνα πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας ὑμᾶς δόξῃ λατρείαν προσφέρειν τῷ Θεῷ.
16:2.targetText: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.

groups.note: The adjective ἀποσυναγώγους ("expelled from the synagogue") with ποιήσουσιν is rendered put … out of the synagogues.
The infinitive προσφέρειν ("to offer") is rendered he is offering.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:3.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα ποιήσουσιν ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸν Πατέρα οὐδὲ ἐμέ.
16:3.targetText: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective καί untranslated.

16:4.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα αὐτῶν μνημονεύητε αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν. ταῦτα δὲ ὑμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς οὐκ εἶπον, ὅτι μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἤμην.
16:4.targetText: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.

groups.note: The genitive αὐτῶν, object of μνημονεύητε ("remember them"), is rendered about them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

16:5.sourceText: νῦν δὲ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐρωτᾷ με Ποῦ ὑπάγεις;
16:5.targetText: Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’

groups.note: Article and participle τὸν πέμψαντα form one unit.

16:6.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ὅτι ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν, ἡ λύπη πεπλήρωκεν ὑμῶν τὴν καρδίαν.
16:6.targetText: Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.

groups.note: The active πεπλήρωκεν ("sorrow has filled") is rendered as the passive are filled with sorrow.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:7.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω ὑμῖν, συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπέλθω. ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ἀπέλθω, ὁ Παράκλητος οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐὰν δὲ πορευθῶ, πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
16:7.targetText: But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.

groups.note: συμφέρει ("it is profitable") is rendered it is for … benefit.
The dative ὑμῖν ("for you") is rendered for your.
The emphatic double negative οὐ μή is rendered not.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

16:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐκεῖνος ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ περὶ κρίσεως·
16:8.targetText: And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment:

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat "in regard to" before righteousness and judgment.

16:9.sourceText: περὶ ἁμαρτίας μέν, ὅτι οὐ πιστεύουσιν εἰς ἐμέ·
16:9.targetText: in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me;

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν, answered by δέ in the next verses, has no English counterpart.

16:10.sourceText: περὶ δικαιοσύνης δέ, ὅτι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ὑπάγω καὶ οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με·
16:10.targetText: in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me;

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

16:11.sourceText: περὶ δὲ κρίσεως, ὅτι ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου κέκριται.
16:11.targetText: and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.

groups.note: κέκριται ("has been judged") is rendered has been condemned.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:12.sourceText: Ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω ὑμῖν λέγειν, ἀλλ’ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι·
16:12.targetText: I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.

groups.note: ἄρτι ("now") is rendered yet.

unmappedTarget.reason: English completes bear with to hear it; βαστάζειν means "to bear".

16:13.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν· οὐ γὰρ λαλήσει ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ὅσα ἀκούει λαλήσει, καὶ τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.
16:13.targetText: However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.

groups.note: The pronoun ἐκεῖνος ("that one"), subject of the coming, is rendered by the He of the main clause.
BSB's Greek text has a slightly different phrase here with the same sense.
BSB's Greek text has another form of this verb.
Article and participle τὰ ἐρχόμενα ("the things coming") form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:14.sourceText: ἐκεῖνος ἐμὲ δοξάσει, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λήμψεται καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.
16:14.targetText: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.

groups.note: ὅτι ("because") is rendered by, with the following verbs as -ing forms.
τοῦ ἐμοῦ ("that which is mine") is rendered what is Mine.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; ἀναγγελεῖ has none.

16:15.sourceText: πάντα ὅσα ἔχει ὁ Πατὴρ ἐμά ἐστιν· διὰ τοῦτο εἶπον ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαμβάνει καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.
16:15.targetText: Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.

groups.note: ἔχει ("has") is rendered belongs to, with the Father as the owner.
διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered That is why.
τοῦ ἐμοῦ ("that which is mine") is rendered what is Mine.
The present λαμβάνει ("takes") is rendered will take.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in "That is why".
BSB names the subject; λαμβάνει has only a verb ending.
English supplies the object; ἀναγγελεῖ has none.

16:16.sourceText: Μικρὸν καὶ οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με.
16:16.targetText: In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me.”

groups.note: μικρόν ("a little") is rendered In a little while.
πάλιν ("again") is rendered then.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί untranslated; the time phrase leads straight into the clause.
BSB leaves καί untranslated; the time phrase leads straight into the clause.

16:17.sourceText: Εἶπαν οὖν ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο ὃ λέγει ἡμῖν Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με; καί Ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα;
16:17.targetText: Then some of His disciples asked one another, “Why is He telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’ and ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”

groups.note: Εἶπαν ("they said") is rendered asked.
Τί ("what") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's asked takes one another as its object, with no word for πρός ("to").
BSB recasts "What is this that He says" as "Why is He telling", leaving ἐστιν τοῦτο ὅ ("is this that") unexpressed.
BSB leaves καί untranslated; the time phrase leads straight into the clause.

16:18.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν Τοῦτο τί ἐστιν ὃ λέγει τὸ μικρόν; οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί λαλεῖ.
16:18.targetText: They kept asking, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’? We do not understand what He is saying.”

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγον ("they were saying") is rendered They kept asking.
τί ("what") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
BSB recasts "What is this that He says" as "Why is He saying", leaving τοῦτο ἐστιν ὅ ("this is that") unexpressed.
The article marks the quoted phrase; BSB quotes it as a little while.

16:19.sourceText: ἔγνω Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤθελον αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾶν, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Περὶ τούτου ζητεῖτε μετ’ ἀλλήλων ὅτι εἶπον Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με;
16:19.targetText: Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, “Are you asking one another why I said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’?

groups.note: ἔγνω ("knew") is rendered Aware.
Περὶ τούτου … ὅτι ("about this … that") is rendered why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns ἔγνω ("knew") into the phrase "Aware that …" and leaves καί untranslated.
BSB's asking takes one another as its object, with no word for μετά ("with").
BSB leaves καί untranslated; the time phrase leads straight into the clause.

16:20.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε ὑμεῖς, ὁ δὲ κόσμος χαρήσεται· ὑμεῖς λυπηθήσεσθε, ἀλλ’ ἡ λύπη ὑμῶν εἰς χαρὰν γενήσεται.
16:20.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι introduces the direct speech and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:21.sourceText: ἡ γυνὴ ὅταν τίκτῃ λύπην ἔχει, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα αὐτῆς· ὅταν δὲ γεννήσῃ τὸ παιδίον, οὐκέτι μνημονεύει τῆς θλίψεως διὰ τὴν χαρὰν ὅτι ἐγεννήθη ἄνθρωπος εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
16:21.targetText: A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.

groups.note: ὅταν τίκτῃ ("when she gives birth") is rendered in childbirth.
οὐκέτι μνημονεύει ("no longer remembers") is rendered forgets.
ἄνθρωπος ("a human being") is rendered a child.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:22.sourceText: καὶ ὑμεῖς οὖν νῦν μὲν λύπην ἔχετε· πάλιν δὲ ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς, καὶ χαρήσεται ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία, καὶ τὴν χαρὰν ὑμῶν οὐδεὶς αἴρει ἀφ’ ὑμῶν.
16:22.targetText: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.

groups.note: The present αἴρει ("takes") is rendered will take.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν, answered by δέ, has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὑμῶν ("from you") unexpressed; your joy already names the owner.

16:23.sourceText: καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἐρωτήσετε οὐδέν. ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἄν τι αἰτήσητε τὸν Πατέρα δώσει ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου.
16:23.targetText: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.

groups.note: ἄν τι ("if … anything") is rendered whatever.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts with "In that day" and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds longer to contrast that day with now; the Greek has a plain οὐκ ("not"), not οὐκέτι.

16:24.sourceText: ἕως ἄρτι οὐκ ᾐτήσατε οὐδὲν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου· αἰτεῖτε, καὶ λήμψεσθε, ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν ᾖ πεπληρωμένη.
16:24.targetText: Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:25.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἐν παροιμίαις λελάληκα ὑμῖν· ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὐκέτι ἐν παροιμίαις λαλήσω ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ παρρησίᾳ περὶ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν.
16:25.targetText: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.

groups.note: ἐν παροιμίαις ("in figures of speech") is rendered this way.

16:26.sourceText: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου αἰτήσεσθε, καὶ οὐ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν Πατέρα περὶ ὑμῶν·
16:26.targetText: In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.

groups.note: περί ("concerning") is rendered on … behalf.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
BSB leaves ὑμῖν ("to you") unexpressed.

16:27.sourceText: αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ φιλεῖ ὑμᾶς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς ἐμὲ πεφιλήκατε καὶ πεπιστεύκατε ὅτι ἐγὼ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον.
16:27.targetText: For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:28.sourceText: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ ἐλήλυθα εἰς τὸν κόσμον· πάλιν ἀφίημι τὸν κόσμον καὶ πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα.
16:28.targetText: I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.”

groups.note: ἐλήλυθα εἰς ("I have come into") is rendered entered.
πάλιν ("again") is rendered In turn.

16:29.sourceText: Λέγουσιν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Ἴδε νῦν ἐν παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖς, καὶ παροιμίαν οὐδεμίαν λέγεις.
16:29.targetText: His disciples said, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.

groups.note: ἐν παρρησίᾳ ("in plainness") is rendered plainly.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not repeat the verb; λέγεις ("You speak") is understood from You are speaking.

16:30.sourceText: νῦν οἴδαμεν ὅτι οἶδας πάντα καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχεις ἵνα τίς σε ἐρωτᾷ· ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν ὅτι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθες.
16:30.targetText: Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.”

groups.note: English repeats that before the second clause, which ὅτι also governs.
Ἄρτι ("now") is rendered finally.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

16:32.sourceText: ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ ἐλήλυθεν ἵνα σκορπισθῆτε ἕκαστος εἰς τὰ ἴδια κἀμὲ μόνον ἀφῆτε· καὶ οὐκ εἰμὶ μόνος, ὅτι ὁ Πατὴρ μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν.
16:32.targetText: “Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.

groups.note: Neuter plural τὰ ἴδια: his own things or home.
κἀμέ (καί + ἐμέ) is rendered and … Me.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds already to bring out the perfect ἐλήλυθεν ("has come").

16:33.sourceText: ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ εἰρήνην ἔχητε. ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἔχετε· ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε, ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον.
16:33.targetText: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!”

groups.note: The present ἔχετε ("you have") is rendered will have.
